30 SPACES / BLOCK 3 STUDY

South/southeast continuation or east of the building?

Blocks 1 and 2 retain their accepted positions in each design. Both candidates use a third 10-space module, five dual-output stations, a 3 × 3 m equipment allowance and proposed pedestrian access. The table compares complete three-block layouts, not Block 3 alone.

Design / candidateLand union / overall boundsIncrement for B3 / vehicle unionB3 door routes E2 / E1Image evidence / site-fit status

South/SE continuation

Continue eastward along the existing south row: Block 3 envelope at (692,360) Standard or (540,360) Compact. Standard repeats the separated end-band logic. Compact adds a second preliminary 1.5 m pedestrian-only passage, extending the 6 m perimeter aisles and moving the outer vehicle end band east. B2 bays, canopy, equipment and door route stay fixed; its eastern vehicle allocation changes in Compact.

Standard puts all B3 stalls beyond the saved image; Compact shows all stalls but its outer end band extends beyond it. A wider diagram canvas shows these areas with a hatched background, not invented terrain. No additional road origin is assumed.

East-side candidate

Block 3 envelope at (476,116), canopy at (564,164), east of the visible building. The 34.5 × 24.5 m module ends at x=752 within the 755 px image. Its west edge is approximately 2 m east of the picked building edge x=460; this is not a verified setback. Its south end connects to the existing 6 m approach at y=312. No new entrance is invented.

Both designs retain full end reservations around this separate east module. Compact here means the accepted compact B1/B2 pair plus an east module, not a claimed compact passage between B2 and B3. Terrain contours, setbacks and servicing remain unverified.

Provisional study priority: east, based on image coverage and the shorter Standard route. This is a comparison of evidence and conceptual geometry, not a feasible-site recommendation. Compact south/SE may use less land, but its off-image outer circulation cannot be checked. No land boundary or available-land polygon is established for either zone.

Shading: possible building shade is unverified in both zones. The east candidate is closer to the building flank and needs particular study; the south-row continuation is farther east. Project North is not verified True North. Recorded building levels do not provide a solar/shadow simulation, and no generation advantage is assigned.

20-SPACE ALTERNATIVES / BOTH UNVERIFIED

Standard versus Compact Design

Accepted 20-space alternatives.

Option A — Standard Design

Accepted M2 arrangement. Block 2 offset: 27 m east. Retains the overlapping inner vehicle end reservations.

Option B — Compact Design

Study only. Block 2 offset: 17.5 m east. Test a pedestrian-only internal gap; use continuous outer vehicle circulation.

ComparisonStandardCompact
Can the inner vehicle reservation be eliminated? Not established. The inherited 11 m end bands support the earlier corner/turning screen; the historical maneuver review still found conflicts. Compact reassigns each affected central inter-block vehicle band (14.5 × 12.5 m = 181.25 m² per interface) to parking and a pedestrian passage; it is no longer vehicle circulation. This affects one interface in the 20-space/east study and two in the three-block south/SE study. Continuous outer aisles establish conceptual connectivity only. Removing the internal crossover may require vehicles to circulate via the outer ends; swept paths, reversing, simultaneous movements and emergency access require new validation. Compact is not approved by the area saving.

Preliminary passage width: 1.5 m. Reused from the accepted pedestrian-spine assumption, not a confirmed accessible-route minimum. The 5 m canopy-to-canopy gap contains the retained 3 m equipment allowance, 0.5 m residual separation and a 1.5 m pedestrian strip. Equipment doors, maintenance, cables, columns and drainage may consume this clearance. The passage crosses both 6 m perimeter aisles at its ends; those crossings remain unresolved.

Block 1’s bays, canopy, equipment and E2 route do not move. Compact changes circulation allocation around them; the original 34.5 × 24.5 m Block 1 reference envelope remains in area accounting. This does not preserve the original maneuvering conditions. Historical maneuver evidence · Conflict review

02 / Land, layout & access

ReservationArea / extentAccounting basis

Axis-aligned rectangle unions at 8 px/m (64 px²/m²). Areas are planning reservations, not surveyed land or paving quantities. Overlap is gross category-union area minus final union; nested equipment and routes are counted once. Shared circulation is a subset, not an extra land charge. Bounding dimensions are not the union area.

Why southeast? The dated Site review identifies an east/southeast study zone. Block 2 stays south of the visible building, close to E2 and the assumed approach, while retaining Block 1. Standard reuses a 7.5 m-wide end reservation; Compact tests closer spacing with an internal pedestrian passage. This is a manually selected conceptual candidate, not a terrain search or certified fit. Its east edge is near the image boundary; land beyond the screenshot is unknown.

Each module retains 2.5 × 5.5 m stalls and a 1.5 m central spine. Standard retains 6 m vehicle aisles and 11 m end reservations. Compact retains 6 m perimeter aisles and 11 m outer end reservations, reassigning the internal vehicle reserve. Five station symbols per spine are schematic; cable reach, bodies, support placement and clear pedestrian width remain unresolved. The inherited 3 × 3 m allowance per block is not a verified station layout.

04 / PROPOSED BIM MATERIAL SPECIFICATIONS

Glulam + engineered timber + PV

POC1 design intent: glulam beams supporting a CLT or suitable engineered-timber deck, with timber or timber/steel hybrid columns, waterproofing, PV mounting rails and modules. Foundations and connections require design.

Proposed roof projection: 12.5 × 12.5 m = 156.25 m², covering the two parking rows and spine. No overhang or panel-packing clearance is established. The section is conceptual, not dimensioned structural design; the 18° PV mounting assumption does not set the timber roof slope.

Existing model materials are not these specifications. Structural adequacy, wind/seismic resistance, fire performance, headroom, accessibility and equipment clearances are not approved. Native family generation, schedules, structural analysis, IFC and carbon accounting remain Phase 2.

How This Design Advisor Works

Two flows, two different responsibilities: historical BIM inspection supplied context; today’s browser calculates and displays conceptual layouts from that saved context.

The Revit MCP tools are operations registered by the TypeScript MCP server, not a second independent server. Revit MCP skills are Markdown workflow guidance used by the inspecting client. The drawing follows the direction of returned information; requests flow toward Revit.

Current behavior: the browser does NOT make live Revit MCP calls when the user switches scenarios. Parking-area, overlap, door-distance and charging calculations run in JavaScript. It does not read the current RVT, test terrain, run swept paths or optimize live BIM.

Revit MCP tools supplied previously inspected model information. Revit MCP skills guided model-query and rule-check workflows; a documented workflow does not establish a successful comprehensive audit. The latest live MCP attempt failed on October 27; M3 uses saved BIM evidence. The 30-space controls compare predefined east and south/SE candidate geometries; they do not optimize live terrain.

Separate POC1 implementation: the C# Revit add-in previously generated canopy geometry in Revit. That generator is not this browser’s calculation engine. Its successful canopy work does not establish site-layout feasibility.

Source-verified path: MCP client ⇄ stdio ⇄ TypeScript/Node server ⇄ WebSocket JSON ⇄ C# plugin ⇄ ExternalEvent / command executor ⇄ Revit API. The source maps query_elements_with_filter to the C# query_elements command. Default port 8964 is a code setting, not a live connectivity assertion. No connection or configuration was tested or changed in M2.1.

Future architectural proposal: automated live BIM-based site optimization would require authorized live data access, terrain and boundary geometry, validated circulation/constraint algorithms and reviewed integration. The dashed future box is not connected to the implemented browser pipeline.

Reference / Energy and charging capacity

Our browser formulas · no solar MCP
Installed PV · DC rating kWp
Annual PV energy · benchmark kWh
Average daily PV energy kWh/day
Full-battery equivalents / day
Partial-charge equivalents / day

/ 10 EV-equipped spaces

simultaneous charging points
Assumed hardware capacity

physical stations

kW aggregate charger demand
Assumed points × kW/point; grid supply unknown

PV energy is not charging power. Annual averages do not guarantee daytime availability or fully charge all connected cars. Grid connection, load sharing, daily throughput, storage and other building loads are unknown. These energy equivalents assume all estimated PV energy is available to charging before the stated charging loss.

Transparent calculation formulas

kWp = panels × W / 1,000; annual kWh = kWp × yield; daily kWh = annual / 365; battery-delivered kWh/day = daily × efficiency / 100. Full-battery equivalents = battery-delivered energy / battery capacity; top-up equivalents = battery-delivered energy / top-up kWh. These are energy equivalents, not promised sessions.

EV-equipped spaces = selected parking capacity (100% EV-equipped in M2); charging points = equipped spaces; physical stations = ceil(points / simultaneous outputs per station). The last station may have unused outputs. Rounding is shown as the actual equipped share. Charger demand = points × assumed kW/point. No grid-supported throughput is calculated.
